intro: Montenegro, the 'Black Mountain', held out in its mountains against the Ottomans for centuries, ruled by prince-bishops. After decades in Yugoslavia it became independent again in 2006.

chapters.title: The mountain state
text: After the medieval states of Duklja and Zeta, the Ottomans conquered most of the Balkans, but Montenegro's clans in their rugged mountains were never fully subdued. From 1696 the Petrović-Njegoš family ruled as prince-bishops, both religious and political leaders. Petar II Petrović-Njegoš wrote the epic poem The Mountain Wreath.
Montenegro's independence was recognised in 1878, and it became a kingdom in 1910.

chapters.title: Yugoslavia and independence
text: In 1918 Montenegro was joined to Serbia and became part of Yugoslavia. When Yugoslavia broke up, it stayed linked with Serbia until a referendum on 21 May 2006, when 55.5% voted for independence, just over the 55% required.
Montenegro joined NATO in 2017 and is among the leading candidates to join the EU.

chapters.title: Montenegro today
text: Montenegro is a small, young state that has grown through tourism, though debates over its identity and its relationship with Serbia continue.

timeline.title: Independence
timeline.text: A referendum ends the union with Serbia.

keyTerms.meaning: A ruler who was also a bishop.
